text.p: Italian debt markets tore up in a last minute rally following a deal between European member states on a stability pact on discipline over budget deficits after economic and monetary union (EMU).
The March Btp future was around 114 basis points higher on the day at 128.47, outgunning its European counterparts, while the July 2006 Btp closed 70 basis points higher at 108.80.

The spread of the 10-year Btp over the 10-year Bund narrowed into a record level of 168 basis points, closer than the 171 record set in November. Traders said they expected the spread to close in gradually to 165 at least in the near term.
The lira hauled itself slightly higher to 985.10/5.60 per mark from around 988 earlier.

Traders, inundated by trade in the wake of the announcement, said some of the bounce was technical after several days of weakness but high yielding Italy was one of the major gainers from the announcement.
While they did not expect Italian rates to fall in the next day or so, some said it was one more reason to cut rates soon.
At home, political factors were overshadowed by the European story. The government called three confidence votes on sections of the 1997 budget bill under scrutiny in the upper house.

The votes were called to sweep aside 3,000 opposition amendments to the bill, which is supposed to pass the final upper house vote by December 19 in order for it to return to the lower house for final approval ahead of its year end deadline.
